title: Dynamic Code Execution and Metaprogramming via send
security_mechanism: eval compiles the string as Ruby source in the current binding, and instance_eval runs it with self bound to the receiver, exposing private state and instance variables of that object to the evaluated text. send and public_send invoke any method chosen by name — public_send excludes private methods but every public destructive method (destroy, update, execute) remains reachable — while class_eval can define or overwrite methods on a class and const_get resolves attacker-chosen names to constants, including class objects. Building an ERB template from input is the same primitive one level up: the template's <%= %> sections are Ruby code that ERB executes during render.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters selecting action/method names, template text, or constant/class names used in dispatch.
source_sink_clues.sink: eval / instance_eval / class_eval on dynamic strings; send / public_send / const_get with input-derived names; ERB.new(attacker_text).result

tracking_guards: Require dispatch through a fixed allowlist hash that maps input keys to constant symbols or callables before any send; require templates to be application-owned files with only data dynamic; require eval to see compile-time constant strings only.
not_candidate_when: The dispatched name is matched against a fixed allowlist of symbols before send, the evaluated string is a constant, or the ERB template comes from a compile-time file and input only supplies render data.
public_references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/470.html
